newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lernout & Hauspie licenses technology to LG Semicon.
newsitem.headline: Lernout & Hauspie licenses technology to LG Semicon.

text.p: Belgian Nasdaq-listed technology firm Lernout & Hauspie (L&H) said on Wednesday it had licensed its automatic speech recognition technology to South Korean semiconductor producer LG Semicon.
L&H said its technology would be integrated into LG Semicon products on the market in early 1997. It gave no financial details.

Seoul-based LG Semicon, a subsidiary of the LG Group, will integrate L&H's automatic speech recognition (ASR) technology into a variety of computer, telecom, automotive and consumer electronics applications.
Future product plans include a multimedia PC that does not require a keyboard, a car navigator system and a robot for use in language education.

The first application will be the Hands Free Phone, a telephone that understands basic verbal commands. It will use L&H's ASR as a word recogniser for dialing, selecting options and answering questions automatically. It will also allow users to check messages verbally without using buttons on the phone.
L&H said last month that Japan's Hitachi had agreed to use its speech products technology.
